1776-1786

Caption This

The American Revolution and Its Ideas

3

How this works (15–20 minutes)

  1. Look at each of the 4 images. Read the “What you’re looking at” line.
  2. Write a short, funny caption, like a meme. Pick a caption style if you want one.
  3. Then write 2–3 sentences about what is really going on. Use at least one key term from the lesson. Type the key term in English, exactly as shown.
  4. Save Progress any time. When all 4 are done, press Finished and upload the file to Canvas.

Keep it respectful: make the joke about the situation, the idea, or the object in the picture. Never joke about soldiers who were hurt or died, children, enslaved or freed people, Native peoples, anyone’s race or religion, or how anyone looks.

Image 1 of 4

Washington leans on a cannon

Not done

What you’re looking at: A painting from Norton Ch. 5 of George Washington. He stands in a dark blue coat with gold shoulder pieces, a yellow vest, a light blue sash, white pants, and tall black boots. He rests one arm on a cannon. A horse and a soldier are behind him. Far away on the left, a line of soldiers walks past a big building. A red flag lies on the ground.

Heads up: This is a real person. Aim your joke at the pose, the cannon, or the situation. Never joke about how he looks.

  • Look at the way he stands. What kind of feeling does the painter want you to have about him?
  • Norton says Washington had only 3,000 soldiers left in December 1776. Why would a win matter so much then?
Pick a caption style (optional)

Key terms that fit this image: HessiansBattle of Trenton (1776)Continental Army
Image 2 of 4

General Burgoyne in his red coat

Not done

What you’re looking at: A painting from Norton Ch. 5 of a British general. He stands in a bright red coat with gold trim, a tan vest, and a dark neck cloth. He rests one hand on the handle of a sword and the other on his hip. Dark storm clouds are behind him, and a tiny battle with smoke is far down in the corner.

Heads up: This is a real person. Aim your joke at the red coat, the sword, the stormy sky, or the surrender. Never joke about how he looks.

  • Look at the red coat and the sword. How does this portrait want you to see him?
  • Norton says Burgoyne’s army was surrounded. Does he look worried here?
Pick a caption style (optional)

Image 3 of 4

A winter camp in the snow

Not done

What you’re looking at: A painting from Norton Ch. 5 of a snowy army camp. Log huts line a snowy path. Two officers in dark blue coats and dark hats walk toward you. Soldiers in worn coats stand beside the huts. An American flag flies on a tall pole.

Heads up: This is a serious one. Many soldiers suffered and died at Valley Forge. Write one clear line about the winter or what it meant. No jokes about the cold, hunger, injuries, or the soldiers.

  • Look at the huts, the snow, and the soldiers’ clothes. What do you think this winter felt like?
  • Norton says Washington’s greatest test of leadership was keeping the army together. Why was that so hard?
Pick a caption style (optional)

Image 4 of 4

Four soldiers, four different looks

Not done

What you’re looking at: A watercolor from Norton Ch. 5. Four soldiers stand in a row on a tan page. Each wears something different. The first has a tall black hat with a feather and a white coat. The second wears a brown coat with a red vest and red pants. The third wears a green hat with feathers and a fringed shirt, and holds a long rifle. The fourth wears a blue coat with red trim and holds a long stick.

Heads up: These are real soldiers from different backgrounds. Aim your joke at the mismatched hats and uniforms. Never joke about anyone’s skin color, looks, or background.

  • Look at the four hats and coats. What do the differences tell you about the army?
  • A young French soldier drew this a few days after the British surrender at Yorktown. Why might he draw the men around him?
